title: THE SUITCASE THAT KEPT COMING BACK
consequences: New local fiction: Len, Orra, Quay Nine and this sorter are authored for this meeting, not recovered player history or species-wide canon.
Keep pickup agreement, actual checks and failures, old route evidence, rule use or non-use, borrowed equipment, any trolley debt and the chosen next question.
All scanner forms are unchanged retained service diagnostics from the-bell-without-a-clapper.json; they do not depict new finished art or the suitcase itself.

rules.name: ONE TRIP / send once, refuse return

scenes.title: THE SUITCASE THAT KEPT COMING BACK
scenes.scene: A green suitcase slides through the pickup hatch. Len, the human porter, reaches for its handle. The belt changes its mind and carries it back into the wall. A moment later it arrives again, wearing the same battered DO NOT THROW tag. Len has put a cushion where it lands. “It was getting personal.”
scenes.ghost: Hello. I’m Friken.Ghost: digital recreation of the developer who built StarDiver and got lost in its infinity. He left me to help keep the place running. Today the place is eating somebody’s luggage with excellent manners. You’re at your own computer on a narrow service channel; Len has the actual hands. I can read the sorter, but I need your judgement before I call an impressive loop a successful delivery. Help us get one case to its owner?

scenes.title: SOMEONE ON THE OTHER SIDE
scenes.scene: Len opens the supervised pickup intercom. A broad three-headed traveller leans toward its camera; one head watches the hatch while another threads a needle. “Orra. The green one is mine. Please leave it shut.” Len explains that he can hand it over with the sorter off, but first needs her destination so the next case does not follow it back.
scenes.ghost: We have a perfectly good human fallback in the fiction: carry the thing. The machine can stay locked out. We also have an owner who has asked for a closed suitcase. No mystery requires us to rummage through her socks.

scenes.title: TWO ARROWS, ONE MOTOR
scenes.scene: On the isolated service bench, Len releases the reader connector. Its OUT and RETURN contacts are latched together. Removing the old plate will prevent another bad read, but this held state also needs clearing. A scrap of tape on the housing reads TEMPORARY FIX; the handwriting is Len’s. He looks at it for a while.
scenes.ghost: There it is. I withdraw my reset-everything plan. We clear this one unloaded relay, preserve the route record, then test one journey. The first uncertain option uses FOCUS: a sample from 0.01 to 20.00 plus your actual attribute against the posted target. The exact band and both consequences are shown before you commit. Looking here has rolled nothing.

scenes.title: THE CASE IS NOT A TEST WEIGHT
scenes.scene: Len finds a steel calibration block beneath the counter. He puts it where the suitcase had been. Orra watches him move the case clear before she resumes sewing. The damaged sorter can be tested, replaced or left isolated. None of those plans needs her coat inside it.
scenes.ghost: I suggested using the luggage because it already had a handle. Len has found a test block, which also has a handle and considerably less invested in this afternoon. We use that. What we learn about an unloaded mechanism will stay an unloaded-mechanism result.

scenes.title: THE EMPTY JOURNEY
scenes.scene: Len disconnects the receiver’s motor output and clips a little lamp across it. Orra’s destination is entered as the end of a single journey. The lamp can tell us whether a command would be sent twice. It cannot certify that a suitcase has arrived.
scenes.ghost: Here’s a rule we can actually keep: ONE TRIP. On the isolated receiver, send one request to the agreed destination, then refuse automatic return. It costs one compute to exercise, recovers one signal and lowers noise by one. It never moves a motor or invents a delivery receipt. We will still need somebody at the far end.

scenes.title: ONE PULSE IS ENOUGH
scenes.scene: The motor output is still disconnected. Len holds the lamp where the camera can see it. A manual request is available alongside the installed rule, so lack of compute cannot trap the job. The calibration block stays on the bench.
scenes.ghost: This is where a new rule earns its name. Exercise ONE TRIP and we retain a real use; choose a manual route and it remains installed but untested. I will not give either route the other’s receipt.

scenes.title: THE HANDLE, AT LAST
scenes.scene: Len sets the closed suitcase on a stationary trolley. The passenger tag is visible; the old station return plate is out of the reader’s path. A strip of red tape keeps the sorter out of service until its separate repair is signed. The job can now leave the counter.
scenes.ghost: We have separated two things I tried to solve with one magnificent button: delivering the luggage and repairing the whole station. One person gets her case today. The station gets an honest repair note. No button gets promoted to management.
